name: Plate-Loaded Hack Squat
source: Official Life Fitness / Hammer Strength Plate-Loaded Hack Squat demonstration (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FioZXSiy98M), level side-view frames at 26.80 s, 28.00 s, and 29.10 s in lifting order. Loaded with one 45 lb (20.41 kg) plate per side (90 lb = 40.82 kg total). Twin linear chrome rails measure 44.9 deg (matching the published 45-degree pressing angle). Bearing friction and dynamic inertia omitted; unloaded carriage starting resistance (125 lbs / 57 kg) recorded separately in base_resistance.

observation.evidence: Three level side-view frames extracted from the official Life Fitness / Hammer Strength Plate-Loaded Hack Squat demonstration (YouTube FioZXSiy98M) at 26.80 s (bottom), 28.00 s (middle), and 29.10 s (top) in lifting order. The carriage holding both the back/shoulder pads and the loading horns slides smoothly along two parallel straight fixed chrome guide rails inclined at ~45 degrees. rail_low and rail_high mark widely separated centerline points along the upper (near-side) chrome guide rail in each pose (camera is tripod-mounted and stationary). One 45 lb (20.41 kg) Hammer Strength Olympic plate is loaded on each side of the carriage (90 lb = 40.823 kg total added plates, verified from the front and close-up shots in the same video). Unloaded carriage starting resistance (125 lbs / 57 kg) is recorded separately in base_resistance from the official Life Fitness product specification.

base_resistance.source: Hammer Strength lists 125 lbs (57 kg) starting resistance for the Plate-Loaded Hack Squat (PL-HSQ2). Constant across linear rail travel.
